claims.text: The compared CrCoNi and Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloys are equiatomic, single-phase FCC materials produced by thermomechanical processing.
Mechanical-property differences between the alloys arise from differences in stacking-fault energy and dislocation behavior.
CrCoNi has lower stacking-fault energy than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
CrCoNi exhibits more uniform dislocation behavior than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
The lower stacking-fault energy and more uniform dislocation behavior of CrCoNi produce more effective strain hardening.
The lower stacking-fault energy and more uniform dislocation behavior of CrCoNi produce greater ductility.
A controlled comparison should test equiatomic CrCoNi against equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
The comparison should use identical room-temperature tensile testing, moderate strain rates, and comparable microstructural states.
The relevant structural mediators are stacking-fault energy, dislocation-core structure, and dislocation interactions.
Lower stacking-fault energy in CrCoNi favors activation of partial dislocations.
Lower stacking-fault energy in CrCoNi promotes dynamic strain hardening.
The greater elemental complexity of the quinary alloy increases local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion in the quinary alloy impedes uniform dislocation motion.
Impeded uniform dislocation motion causes less homogeneous plastic deformation and earlier strain localization in the quinary alloy.
CrCoNi will exhibit higher strain hardening than the quinary alloy under identical test conditions.
CrCoNi will exhibit higher ductility and more homogeneous deformation than the quinary alloy under identical test conditions.
The proposed trend applies at ambient temperature and standard strain rates but may not apply at extreme temperatures or very high strain rates.
TEM deformation-substructure analysis can indirectly estimate stacking-fault energy and identify the expected dislocation-structure differences.
